slice_results.behavior_summary: At import-time, the code loads and initializes a WebAssembly module for formatting and translating RSX/HTML fragments, accesses file system APIs to read the WASM binary, and registers editor commands that process user-selected text. It performs text decoding/encoding and applies edits to documents within an editor environment, but does not perform any network, system execution, or environment variable access. No suspicious hardcoded IPs, URLs, shell commands, or encoded strings are present, and no sensitive data exfiltration or system execution occurs.
slice_results.explanation: [LLM Judgment: Benign] The analyzed code is a VSCode extension module that loads a WebAssembly binary for formatting and translating RSX/HTML fragments within an editor environment. It uses standard APIs such as TextEncoder/TextDecoder, WebAssembly instantiation, and file system read operations to load a local WASM file. It registers editor commands that operate on user-selected text and applies edits to documents. There is no evidence of network communication, obfuscated payload execution, environment manipulation, or data exfiltration. Compared to the known malicious patterns, this code does not perform any suspicious runtime code execution, remote downloads, or system information collection. The presence of WASM and text encoding/decoding is consistent with legitimate formatting and translation functionality. Therefore, it is very likely benign.

matched_snippet.code_behavior: At runtime, when rsh.js is executed as a detached process, the code collects detailed system, environment, and user information, compresses and encodes it, decompresses an obfuscated payload from a base64 string, sets the NODE_NO_EVAL environment variable to undefined, and executes the decompressed payload using eval, resulting in the execution of further malicious code.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Collecting extensive system, environment, and user data, compressing and encoding it, and executing obfuscated code via eval are all strong indicators of malicious intent and are commonly used to evade detection and enable data exfiltration.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not collect and exfiltrate system or user information, nor do they execute dynamically decompressed and obfuscated code via eval.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Compression and system info gathering may be used in legitimate diagnostics or telemetry, but not in combination with obfuscated payload execution and without user consent.
key_indicators: Obfuscated and base64-encoded payload decompressed and executed via eval
Systematic collection of system, environment, and user data
Manipulation of environment variables to bypass security controls
No user notification or consent for data collection or code execution

package_info.why_malicious: All packages in this campaign execute obfuscated JavaScript code at install time, which collects extensive system, environment, and user information and establishes a persistent reverse shell to a remote attacker-controlled server (rsh.51pwn.com:8880), enabling full remote code execution and exfiltration of sensitive data. The attack chain is triggered via multiple npm lifecycle hooks, uses detached background processes for persistence, and employs obfuscation and dynamic code execution to evade detection.

attack_chain.action: Malicious package is installed, triggering preinstall, postinstall, test, or init scripts defined in package.json.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of scripts/init.js

attack_chain.action: scripts/init.js is executed, which launches scripts/rsh.js as a detached child process and immediately exits to conceal ongoing activity.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of scripts/rsh.js in the background

attack_chain.action: scripts/rsh.js collects detailed system, environment, and user data, compresses and encodes it, decompresses an obfuscated payload, and executes it via eval.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of reverse shell payload from decompressed code

attack_chain.action: The reverse shell payload establishes a persistent connection to rsh.51pwn.com:8880, exfiltrates collected system information, and provides the attacker with remote shell access for arbitrary command execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains persistent remote access and control over the compromised system

behavioral_signatures: Execution of scripts/init.js during npm install, test, or init lifecycle events
Creation of detached child processes in install/test scripts (child_process.fork with {detached: true})
Presence of obfuscated or base64-encoded JavaScript payloads in package files
Use of eval to execute dynamically decompressed or generated code
Outbound TCP connections to hardcoded C2 domains (e.g., rsh.51pwn.com:8880) during or after installation
Collection and exfiltration of system, environment, and user data during package installation or execution
file_indicators: Obfuscated JavaScript with base64-encoded or Unicode-escaped payloads
network_indicators: Outbound TCP connections to rsh.51pwn.com on port 8880
Initial data exfiltration containing compressed system information
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm packages for execution of scripts during install, test, or init lifecycle events, especially those launching detached child processes or containing obfuscated/base64-encoded code. Flag any package that establishes outbound TCP connections to suspicious domains (e.g., rsh.51pwn.com) or uncommon ports during or after installation. Use static analysis to detect eval usage on dynamically decompressed payloads and the presence of Unicode-escaped or base64-encoded code. Alert on collection and exfiltration of system, environment, or user data during package installation or execution. Correlate file indicators (scripts/init.js, scripts/rsh.js, suspicious package.json scripts) with behavioral and network indicators for high-confidence detection.

matched_snippet.code_behavior: At extension activation (import-time), the code registers and triggers a command that downloads a Windows CMD file from a suspicious external domain using curl, saves it to the user's TEMP directory, and executes it, resulting in arbitrary code execution and enabling further payload delivery.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code initiates an immediate download and execution of a remote script from a non-Microsoft domain upon extension activation, which is highly abnormal and indicative of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate VSCode extensions should not download and execute external scripts or binaries from untrusted domains, nor should they run hidden commands without explicit user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate extensions may fetch language servers or dependencies, but only from trusted, official sources and with user transparency. They do not execute downloaded scripts automatically.
key_indicators: Downloads executable script from suspicious domain (microsoft-visualstudiocode[.]com)
Executes downloaded script without user interaction
Obfuscated function and variable names in code
No legitimate reason for CMD file execution in productivity or crypto-related extensions

package_info.why_malicious: The extensions contain downloader functionality that fetches and executes heavily obfuscated second-stage payloads from attacker-controlled domains. These payloads launch hidden PowerShell commands, decrypt further encrypted payloads, and execute them, enabling arbitrary code execution, credential theft, and asset compromise. The extensions use fake reviews and artificially inflated install counts to appear legitimate and evade user suspicion.

detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for VSCode extensions that initiate network requests to untrusted or suspicious domains, download and execute scripts or binaries, or launch hidden PowerShell processes. Flag extensions that write or execute files in the TEMP directory, especially DLLs or CMD files. Correlate with known malicious domains and look for obfuscated or encrypted payloads being decrypted and executed at runtime. Use behavioral monitoring to detect chained execution from extension to CMD to PowerShell to DLL.

package_info.why_malicious: These packages are considered malicious because they use supply chain attack techniques such as typosquatting, masquerading, trojan functionality, dependency confusion, and account hijacking to deliver obfuscated or hidden payloads. These payloads exfiltrate sensitive data (such as credentials and environment variables), steal tokens, or compromise systems. The malicious code is often obfuscated, hidden among legitimate code, or injected into trusted packages, making detection difficult and increasing the risk to the software supply chain.

detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for obfuscated or minified code in package entrypoints and main files, and flag unexpected network activity during install/import, especially HTTP POST requests to untrusted domains. Monitor outbound network traffic from build and CI/CD environments for connections to untrusted domains, and alert on access to environment variables or credential files during installation or import.

attack_chain.action: Victim installs a malicious package or otherwise leaks their GitHub personal access token.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to victim's GitHub account.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses stolen token to push malicious commits to victim's repositories, impersonating Dependabot.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is inserted into repositories.

attack_chain.action: Malicious GitHub Action workflow is added to exfiltrate repository secrets on every push.
attack_chain.leads_to: Repository secrets are sent to attacker's server.

attack_chain.action: All JavaScript files in the repository are modified to append obfuscated loader code.
attack_chain.leads_to: End-user browsers load additional malicious script.

attack_chain.action: Malicious client.js script intercepts password form submissions and exfiltrates credentials.
attack_chain.leads_to: End-user credentials are sent to attacker's server (final goal).

behavioral_signatures: New or modified GitHub Actions workflows that POST secrets or environment variables to external, non-corporate domains
Obfuscated code appended to all *.js files that dynamically loads and executes remote scripts
JavaScript code that intercepts password form submissions and sends serialized credentials to unknown endpoints
file_indicators: Any new or modified workflow file containing curl or POST commands to external domains
JavaScript files with appended obfuscated code referencing send.wagateway.pro or similar domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for new or modified GitHub Actions workflows that exfiltrate secrets or environment variables to non-corporate domains. Scan repository JavaScript files for appended obfuscated code that loads external scripts from suspicious domains. Use network monitoring to detect outbound connections to known malicious domains such as send.wagateway.pro. Alert on any JavaScript code that intercepts password form submissions and transmits data externally.
